 Judgment

The appellants have filed the present miscellaneous second appeal against the judgment and award dated 27.01.2016 passed in LACA No.241/2015 on the file of the IV Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi, whereby compensation of Rs.1,68,762/- per acre for dry land with all statutory benefits, was awarded.

sentences.text: It is the case of the appellants that they are the joint owners of the land bearing Survey No.224/1 measuring 22 guntas and the land bearing Survey No.220/3 measuring 6 acre 29 guntas, totally 7 acre 9 guntas, situate at Karadal Village of Chittapur Taluka, Kalaburagi District.

The respondents acquired the said lands for the purpose of Minor Irrigation Project by issuing notification dated 22.12.1993 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, followed by final notification and common award came to passed on 15.02.1996 fixing market value of Rs.11,000/- per acre for dry land, based on sales statistics method.

Being not satisfied with the NC: 2024:KHC-K:2160 award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, the appellants filed an application under Section 18(1) of the Land Acquisition Act before Special Land Acquisition Officer for reference.
Upon reference, the reference Court considering the entire material on record, by common judgment and award dated 27.10.2003 awarded compensation of Rs.31,150/- per acre with all statutory benefits.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award passed by the reference Court, the appellants preferred an appeal in LACA No.241/2015.
The first Appellate Court, considering the material on record, enhanced the market value at Rs.1,68,762/- per acre with all statutory benefits.
Being not satisfied with the compensation awarded by the first Appellate Court, the present appeal is filed for enhancement of the compensation.
3. I have heard the learned counsels for the parties to the lis.

Sri S.S. Sajjanshetty, the learned counsel for the appellants would vehemently contend that the judgment and award passed by the first Appellate Court awarding compensation of Rs.1,68,762/-
per acre for dry land is on the lower side and is without any basis.

He would further contend that this Court in MSA No.200010/2017 (LAC) dated 22.03.2018 having awarded compensation of Rs.1,82,262/- per acre for dry land with all statutory benefits, the same has to be applied to the facts and circumstances of the present case, since, the notification issued and the purpose are one and the same.
On are these grounds sought for enhancement of compensation by modifying the judgment and award of the first Appellate Court.

5. Per contra, learned HCGP Sri Gopalkrishna B. Yadav sought to justify the impugned judgment and award passed by the first Appellate Court awarding compensation of Rs.1,68,762/- per acre with all statutory benefits, contending that in the absence of any material on record, NC:
2024:KHC-K:2160 the first Appellate Court is justified in awarding the impugned compensation,
which is just and proper and there are no grounds for interference by this Court under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act.
Therefore, he sought for dismissal of the appeal.
6. I have heard learned counsels for both the parties.

It is an undisputed fact that the land of the appellants measuring 7 acre 09 guntas situated at Kardal Village was acquired by the respondents for Minor Irrigation Project by issuing preliminary notification dated 22.12.1993 and the Special Land Acquisition Officer has fixed market value of the acquired land at Rs.11,000/- per acre and the same was modified by the Reference Court to Rs.31,150/- per acre with all statutory benefits.
The first Appellate Court, considering the material on record, has proceeded to award Rs.1,68,762/- per acre for dry land with all statutory benefits.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the case of the appellants before this Court that in an identical circumstance in LACA No.183/2014 in respect of the same notification for the same purpose, for the lands acquired in Kardal Village, the first Appellate Court has awarded compensation at Rs.1,82,262/- per acre for dry land and the said judgment and award in LACA No.183/2014 having reached finality, acquisition is the first Appellate Court ought to have considered and passed appropriate orders in accordance with law.

It is also not in dispute that the land acquired in LACA No.183/2014 and the lands acquired in the present case are under different notification, which is 09 [nine] days prior, but acquisition is for the same purpose.
There cannot be any discrimination between the parties for payment of compensation, when notification issued and the award passed are the one and the same.
Unfortunately, it was not brought to the notice of the first Appellate Court about the judgment passed in LACA No.183/2014.
In view of the aforesaid reasons, the appeal is allowed in part with costs.

The impugned judgment and award passed in LACA No.241/2015 on the file of the IV Additional District and Sessions Judge is modified holding that the appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.1,82,262/- per acre for dry land, with all statutory benefits.

9. It is made clear that the appellants are not entitled to any interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period of 891 days in filing the appeal, as per order passed by this Court dated 06.08.2021.
